audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for Ethereum Execution Layer focusing on external entities that interact with the EL through various interfaces.

misclassified_entities.reason: Client implementation teams do not interact with the running system at runtime; they develop the software. Not a runtime external entity.
Core developers do not interact with the running system at runtime; they define protocol changes through governance. Not a runtime external entity.
EIP authors do not interact with the running system at runtime. Not a runtime external entity.

The beacon deposit contract at 0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa is a smart contract executing within the EVM, making it an internal component, not an external entity. However, its outputs (deposit events) are consumed by the CL, creating a trust boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operators
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Node deployment, configuration, and P2P network participation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators run EL clients and participate in P2P networking. They are untrusted in the Byzantine fault tolerant model - the protocol assumes up to f < n/3 nodes can be malicious, misconfigured, or compromised. The system must maintain safety and liveness despite malicious operators.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers propagate blocks via unauthenticated P2P protocol. Peers may be Byzantine actors attempting to propagate invalid blocks, cause DoS, or exploit consensus bugs. All blocks must undergo full validation: header, PoW/PoS, state transitions, and merkle roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender (EOA)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Signed transactions via P2P gossip or JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction senders are externally owned accounts that sign transactions. While ECDSA signatures provide authentication, senders are untrusted and may attempt malicious transactions, reentrancy, or resource exhaustion. The EL validates nonces, balances, gas limits, and executes in sandboxed EVM with gas metering.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Miner (PoW)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners produce blocks and select transactions in PoW networks (Homestead). They are untrusted and may attempt censorship, MEV extraction, transaction reordering, or invalid state transitions. PoW provides Sybil resistance but all block content must be validated by full nodes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Consensus Layer (beacon chain) communicates with the Execution Layer via Engine API using JWT authentication. The channel is authenticated, establishing identity, but the content requires validation. The CL proposes execution payloads (blocks) and fork choice updates. The EL must validate all payload content: transaction validity, state transitions, gas limits, and consensus rules. A compromised or buggy CL should not cause the EL to accept invalid state.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Node configuration and P2P network participation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Node operators are untrusted participants in a Byzantine fault tolerant system. The protocol assumes up to f < n/3 nodes can be malicious. Consensus safety is maintained through validation rules and cryptographic verification that honest nodes enforce.

Network peers are untrusted and may be Byzantine actors. All blocks undergo full validation: header structure validation, PoW/PoS verification (depending on fork), transaction execution, state root computation and verification, receipt root verification, and gas limit checks. Invalid blocks are rejected and peers may be penalized.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction processing pipeline (mempool and block execution)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transaction senders are untrusted. The EL enforces: (1) ECDSA signature verification for authentication, (2) sender account must be EOA (no code), (3) nonce must match current account nonce, (4) balance >= gas*gasPrice + value, (5) transaction execution in isolated EVM context with gas metering, stack depth limits, and memory limits.

Miners are untrusted block producers in PoW. The EL validates: (1) PoW solution via hashimoto_light algorithm, (2) difficulty target meets network difficulty, (3) block header fields (gas limit, timestamp, parent hash), (4) all transactions are valid and executable, (5) state root matches computed state after execution, (6) gas used and receipts match execution results. Miners can only propose blocks; all nodes independently validate.

The CL is semi-trusted with authenticated channel (JWT) but untrusted content. The Engine API uses JWT to authenticate the CL's identity, preventing unauthorized access. However, the EL must validate all payload content from the CL: (1) execution payloads undergo full transaction validation, (2) state transitions are computed and verified, (3) gas limits are enforced, (4) fork choice updates are validated for consistency with known chain state, (5) deposit requests extracted from logs are validated for correct format and source contract.
